say: Iron Man is coming back to Marvel. As the villain.
Before Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters on December eighteenth, here's every movie you need, in order.
It starts in 2000, with the X-Men.
Professor X wants mutants and humans to live in peace. His old friend Magneto wants mutants on top.
Remember these faces. Twenty-six years later, they're coming back.
In 2008, Tony Stark builds a suit of armor in a cave, and Marvel builds a whole universe around him.
A super soldier wakes up from the ice. A god of thunder falls from the sky.
And in 2012, they team up as the Avengers, to stop Thor's brother Loki and an alien army over New York.
Then [Thanos](/θˈɑnOs/) collects all six Infinity Stones, snaps his fingers, and half of all life turns to dust.
In Endgame, the survivors travel back in time, steal the stones, and bring everyone home.
Tony snaps [Thanos](/θˈɑnOs/) away, and dies a hero. Steve Rogers stays in the past, to finally have that dance with Peggy Carter.
But during the time heist, the 2012 Loki grabs the Tesseract, and vanishes.
He gets arrested by the TVA, an office that deletes any timeline that goes off script.
At the end of time, his variant Sylvie kills the man in charge, and one timeline explodes into infinite universes.
To save them all, Loki takes a throne at the end of time, and holds the multiverse together.
In No Way Home, a spell goes wrong. Villains from other universes pour in, along with two more Spider-Men.
To close the door, the whole world forgets Peter Parker ever existed.
Doctor Strange learns the scariest word in the multiverse: incursion. When two universes collide, both are destroyed.
[Shuri](/ʃˈʊɹi/) becomes the new Black Panther, and meets [Namor](/nˈAmɔɹ/), king of an underwater empire.
Ant-Man and his daughter Cassie get pulled into the Quantum Realm, and fight an exiled conqueror.
In The Marvels, Monica [Rambeau](/ɹæmbˈO/) gets stranded in another universe, and wakes up next to Beast, from the X-Men.
Over in the old X-Men universe, Deadpool learns his world is dying, because its Wolverine is dead.
So he drags in the worst Wolverine in the multiverse, survives the Void, where forgotten heroes like Gambit end up, and saves his world.
Sam Wilson is Captain America now. He stops a giant Red Hulk, who happens to be the President, and decides to rebuild the Avengers.
Meanwhile, Yelena, Bucky and a team of misfits save New York from Bob, a hero with the power of a million exploding suns, and a darkness that turns people into shadows.
Fun fact: the asterisk in [Thunderbolts*](/θˈʌndəɹbˌOlts/) is real. It stands for, The New Avengers.
Fourteen months later, a ship from another universe arrives, with a big four on the side.
That's the Fantastic Four, from Earth [828](/ˈAt twˈɛnti ˈAt/), a retro-future world.
They beat [Galactus](/ɡəlˈæktəs/), a planet eater who wanted their baby son, Franklin.
But four years later, someone comes to visit little Franklin. Someone in a metal mask.
And in Brand New Day, a forgotten Peter Parker faces a grieving young telepath named Jean Grey, and talks a raging Hulk back down.
Which brings us to Doomsday. The multiverse is collapsing, and Doctor Doom is standing right in the middle of it.
Heroes from three universes, the Avengers, the Fantastic Four, and the X-Men, have to fight side by side.
Steve Rogers is back. Thor is back. Professor X and Magneto are back.
And under Doom's mask? Robert Downey Junior. The man who started it all, as Iron Man.
Avengers: Doomsday. December eighteenth.
